name: Kawagiri 川霧 restaurant (deck and pods over the river)
purpose: Dinner behind falling water: guests cross a gangway between two water curtains onto a long deck over the fast teal river, and each party disappears into its own lantern-lit pod while soy and tea arrive by tiny wooden aqueducts.

ceiling_profile.note: Raw basalt vault, wet and black, lowest (-32) over the north bank and the lift drum, highest (-28) over the middle of the river. No roof over the spine deck so the curtains and the neon gate read against the dark rock; each pod has its own low hinoki roof (top about -36.8) carrying its ceiling trough.

portals.note: Main way in. Clear opening 4.0 m between two noren posts inside the 6 m layout opening, 3 m high: the compressed threshold before the deck reveal.
Ramen-side way in/out; the counter's neon is framed through it.

branches.why: West end of the deck: overlook downstream toward the falls mist.
East end of the deck: under the sign gate.

hero.why: The deck is a 60 m straight vista and needs a terminus or the eye runs off into the dark. A heavy hinoki gate spans the east end of the deck carrying the 川霧 kanji in hand-bent magenta neon with a cyan crest (both faces lit, so it also reads from the boat landing), and its cross-beam carries the soy/tea aqueduct over the river from the kitchen header. It is the brightest thing in the space, the only large neon, and every lantern row on the deck converges on it.

anchored.why: Sparse hinoki slatted deck (12 cm boards, 6 cm gaps) across the walking direction, so the river rushes visibly underfoot (owner request). The spine deck on heavy posts and cross-braced beams standing in the river (concepts 06, 07). Piers sit on basalt footings; spacing 6 m so piers never land on pod gaps' sightlines to the water.

Sparse hinoki slatted deck (12 cm boards, 6 cm gaps) across the walking direction, so the river rushes visibly underfoot (owner request). Main gangway from the core across 8 m of water between T7 and T8; curtains fall 1.3-2.1 m either side of you.
Sparse hinoki slatted deck (12 cm boards, 6 cm gaps) across the walking direction, so the river rushes visibly underfoot (owner request). East gangway between T11 and T12, back to the ramen counter.

North row pod T6 on beams over the river; open side and step face the spine deck, water curtains on the other three sides, aqueduct spouts at the back.
South row pod T7 on beams over the river; open side faces the spine deck. Flanks the main gangway (x 68.5-71.5) so guests walk out between two curtains.
South row pod T8 on beams over the river; open side faces the spine deck. Flanks the main gangway (x 68.5-71.5) so guests walk out between two curtains.

South row pod T9 on beams over the river; open side faces the spine deck. Row breaks at x 84-96 for the lift drum (r 8, cut out of this footprint at r 8.4) which stands in the river here, as the plan's gap between T9 and T10.

South row pod T10 on beams over the river; open side faces the spine deck. Row breaks at x 84-96 for the lift drum (r 8, cut out of this footprint at r 8.4) which stands in the river here, as the plan's gap between T9 and T10.
South row pod T11 on beams over the river; open side faces the spine deck. Flanks the east gangway (x 108.5-111.5).
South row pod T12 on beams over the river; open side faces the spine deck. Flanks the east gangway (x 108.5-111.5).

Soy and genmaicha run by gravity from the header tanks above the kitchen, over the river on the sign gate's beam, then west on thin stilts behind the north pods (1:20 fall) with a branch and sluice gate to every table (07, 08). The proxy is the T4 branch: it comes through the pod's back wall onto the chef_table at table height (concept 08).

South network behind T7-T12; between T9 and T10 it is bracketed to the river face of the lift drum (two corners lie 0.2 m inside the drum cut-out, on the drum wall), which makes the drum part of the restaurant instead of an obstacle.
Small vertical neon on the north bank rock between T2 and T3, seen across the pods from the deck (06 left).
Cyan vertical sign between T4 and T5 (06 centre); neon stays small and paired with dark rock.
One blossom tree on the north bank behind the gate, lit magenta from below (06 top left): it backs the hero.
Closes the west end of the deck as an overlook toward the falls.
Solid lit sign panel on the gate's cross-beam (review r1 top change): the vista ends on the brightest thing.
Low hinoki table in each pod (08).
Pod platforms are slatted too (boards across the step-in direction): diners see the river under the table. Chosen over a solid table zone: the table itself reads as the solid island.
South-row pod platforms, slatted.

water.note: Owned by b2_river (listed here so pods and piers know the surface). Deck -40 is about 2.5-2.9 m above the water.
Water curtains fall from each pod's ceiling trough past the floor gutter straight into the river (07 section A-A). They part for a few seconds when a server steps up.

sightlines.see: Down a 3 m gangway between the T7 and T8 curtains; across the deck T1 and T2 glow behind their own curtains; mist on the river below.
East along the deck: pods both sides, red chochin pools and dark gaps, ending in the neon 川霧 gate.
Downstream over the Mist Steps' water sheets to the white plume rising off the Thunder Curtain lip.
Through the east gangway: the ramen counter's magenta neon and steam (next space's light).
East up the river to the boardwalk lanterns and the boat landing glow.

entry.note: Off the main gangway onto the deck, turning east: the gate closes the vista.

reveal.note: From the east gangway landing looking back west: both pod rows and their curtains converge down the deck.

concept.match: Inside the T4 chef_table pod: wet dark hinoki table in the foreground, the arched aqueduct with its sluice spout pouring soy into a dish and tea into a cup, the water curtain behind lit magenta/cyan, a small andon lantern, steam.

down.note: Looking down about 35 deg on the spine between T3 and T9: teal river and white water through the deck gaps.

lights.note: Brightest source: neon 川霧 (magenta) + crest (cyan), both faces.

lights.why: Red chochin at the deck-side corners of each pod (06): each pod is a pool of light; the 1-11 m gaps between pods stay darker.
One low post at each pod gap midpoint (north 5, south 3): pools at the pods, dark gaps between, a beat that runs to the gate.
Pairs marking where each gangway lands on the deck.

lights.role: warm washi panel glow inside each pod behind its curtain
lights.note: Part of kawagiri_pod; backlights the curtain so it reads as a glowing sheet from the deck and from the river.

dressing.skip_at: pod steps (x = pod centre +-1.2) and gangways
dressing.why: Deck south edge rail (posts every 1.5 m), open at each pod step and gangway.
Main gangway rail, west; T7 curtain beyond.
Main gangway rail, east; T8 curtain beyond.
Short noren over each pod's deck-side opening (06); the server parts it with the curtain.
T1-T12 table boards on each pod's front post (07).
North bank ledge: wet black rock, ferns between.
Two dark silhouettes on the north bank between pod backs, against the curtain glow.
One small table lantern per pod, on the table (08).

mood.key: neon 川霧 gate at the end of the deck; curtains glowing between red chochin
mood.palette: red chochin + amber washi, magenta and cyan neon (only here and in b2_core), teal river glow from below, black wet basalt, aged hinoki
mood.mist: Dense low mist on the river under the deck, thin wisps rising between pods; none on the deck itself.

waivers.reason: Pods repeat at a near-regular pitch on purpose (a restaurant row, as in 06/07); the irregular gap for the lift drum and the gangways breaks the grid.
